guide.title: the protocols
guide.intro: Three paths to lay down. Each follows a different rhythm — but all slow down deliberately. The oracle needs time to listen.
guide.footer: protocols inspired by a living library

reve.title: The dream
reve.intro: Welcoming a dream means letting it speak before wanting it to say. The protocol deliberately slows down — because the logical brain, if left to itself, crushes everything sensory, vague, symbolic.

steps.name: Welcome
steps.desc: Replay the dream like a film. No analysis yet. The logical brain crushes sensory details if allowed in too early.

steps.name: Body
steps.desc: The felt sense (Gendlin). The overall emotion lives in the body before it has a name. Where does it settle — throat, belly, shoulders?

steps.name: Figures
steps.desc: Who is there? People, presences, animals, silhouettes. Hillman insists: stay with the image. Don't translate it into concept.

steps.name: Place
steps.desc: Where it happens. A familiar place distorted, an invented space — both count. The dream chooses its setting for a reason.

steps.name: Action
steps.desc: What happens, in the order it happens. Resist the urge to summarize. Seemingly insignificant details are often the heart of the dream.

steps.name: Question
steps.desc: What question does the dream seem to be asking? Moss calls it 'the dream's invitation'. Not an interpretation — an invitation.

steps.name: Resonances
steps.desc: The AI crosses with your past dreams and day events. Patterns emerge over time.

steps.name: Detail
steps.desc: A singular fragment that struck you — to note separately. It's often through this detail that the dream will speak to you later.

steps.name: Title
steps.desc: Name it. A three to five word title — to find it again, and to give it a shape that holds.

jour.title: The day
jour.intro: The day journal is the inverse of the dream: the conscious mind lays down, so night can work on it. Five short steps.

steps.name: Crossing
steps.desc: What moved through you today — emotion, thought, encounter. Naming an experience disarms its charge.

steps.name: Shift
steps.desc: A moment when something changed — micro or grand. This is often where the unconscious hooks in.

steps.name: Resonance
steps.desc: What still resonates, right now, in your body. If you feel nothing — that's a valid answer.

steps.name: Figure
steps.desc: A presence that returned — person, symbol, motif. Day figures often prepare dream figures.

steps.name: Intention
steps.desc: What you set for the night. Not a precise request — a direction.

rituel.title: The ritual
rituel.intro: The pre-sleep ritual prepares the dream terrain. It's not magic — it's a body protocol that tells the brain: the day is over, you can let go.

steps.name: Arrival
steps.desc: How you arrive at night. The present state, unfiltered. Reverie begins with accepting what is.

steps.name: Question
steps.desc: A question to ask the night — what you want it to work on. Open phrasing, leaving room.

steps.name: Anchoring
steps.desc: A body gesture. Three breaths, hand on the sternum, a candle blown out. The body remembers transitions better than the mind.

steps.name: Laying down
steps.desc: What you leave to the day — what you don't take to sleep. Receiving the night means leaving space for it.

steps.name: Crossing
steps.desc: A phrase to yourself, silent or whispered. Not an affirmation — an agreement.
